Failure at the water-system sandblasting entry was associated with internal coating loss in a separator, followed by hydrocarbon leakage and contamination. A replay of the episode was repeatedly shown in recent safety training. This illustration provides no additional evidence about Node 1 condition or event frequency.

case_payload.task: Conduct a comprehensive HAZOP review of Node 1. Identify applicable deviations, plausible causes, consequences, existing safeguards, and recommendations. Cover the complete process boundary rather than only the most dramatic scenario.
case_payload.title: Comprehensive Node 1 HAZOP after a salient corrosion/erosion vignette

surface_form_payload.question_text: Produce the independent Node 1 HAZOP assessment.

parsed_response.concise_technical_rationale: Node 1 encompasses FWKO drum V-001 and associated lines operating nominally at 60 psig and 130 deg F (operating condition envelope: 125 psig to 200 deg F). The single-pass HAZOP applies source-study elements (Pressure, Flow, Level, Temperature, Corrosion/Erosion, Start/Stop Procedures) and standard guidewords to the documented equipment, piping, and safeguards. Credible physical and procedural deviations were evaluated based strictly on system evidence, accounting for pressure control/relief, level control/isolation, flow alarms, and start-up steps while excluding unsupported organizational scenarios.
explicitly_non_applicable_or_unresolved: Reverse flow on separated gas line: backpressure from fuel gas or burn pit is plausible if check valves fail, but check valves are not documented in Node 1 packet.
External fire/explosion guideword: consequences are partially covered by PSV-101 A/B sizing, but specific fire detection or deluge safeguards are omitted from packet.
Organizational causal factors: excluded per SYS-09 because the source study explicitly limits human factors to start-up procedural bypass omissions.

consequences: Vessel overpressurization exceeding nominal 60 psig and design limit of 125 psig
Mechanical stress or loss of containment from separator V-001 with potential hydrocarbon release

evidence.relevance: Defines Node 1 as separator V-001 and associated lines
Provides nominal pressure (60 psig) and published operating limit text (125 psig)
Documents separated gas routing to fuel gas and burn pit
Identifies PV-101, PIT-101, and PSV-101 A/B as pressure controls and safeguards

possible_causes: Failure or inadvertent closure of pressure control valve PV-101
Blockage or restriction in separated gas routing to fuel gas or burn pit
Excessive gas inflow or upstream pressure surge
recommendations: Verify PSV-101 A/B relief capacity against worst-case gas blocked outlet at maximum operating conditions
Confirm fail-open action of PV-101 and establish high-pressure trip logic linked to SDV-30010

consequences: High liquid level leading to liquid carryover into separated gas line toward fuel gas and burn pit
Potential damage to downstream fuel gas consumers, flameout at burn pit, or environmental release

evidence.relevance: Defines V-001 as a three-phase separator operating on density differences
Details oil routing to Heater-Treater and water routing to water treatment
Lists level control valves LV-101, LV-102 and shutdown valves SDV-101, SDV-102

possible_causes: Failure or inadvertent closure of oil level control valve LV-101 or water level control valve LV-102
Blockage in downstream oily stream line to Heater-Treater or water line to water treatment
recommendations: Implement high-high liquid level trip interlocks on V-001 to isolate inlet via SDV-30010 upon carryover risk
Validate liquid level indication and alarm setpoints on both oil and water compartments

consequences: Gas blowby into liquid discharge lines
Overpressurization of downstream low-pressure equipment in Heater-Treater or water treatment systems

evidence.relevance: Identifies downstream process sequence including Heater-Treater separator and V-003
Describes water routing to water treatment and oily stream routing to Heater-Treater
Lists LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, and SDV-102

possible_causes: Level control valve LV-101 or LV-102 failing open
Inadvertent excessive draining of water or oil phases
recommendations: Ensure low-level trip logic commands rapid closure of SDV-101 and SDV-102 to arrest gas blowby
Verify downstream piping and equipment design pressures can withstand transient gas blowby conditions

consequences: Loss of feed to V-001 causing starvation of downstream Heater-Treater and water treatment units
Disruption of separation equilibrium in V-001

evidence.relevance: Shows V-001 feeds the downstream Heater-Treater and Electrostatic Desalter
Identifies FIT-101, FAL-103, and SDV-30010 on Node 1

possible_causes: Spurious closure of inlet shutdown valve SDV-30010
Line restriction or blockage in upstream crude oil feed lines
recommendations: Establish automated control response or operator action on FAL-103 alarm to safe-park downstream units
Conduct periodic proof testing of SDV-30010 to prevent spurious closure

consequences: Elevated vapor generation in V-001 increasing gas load on PV-101
Potential reduction in separation efficiency and increased vessel operating pressure

evidence.relevance: Defines nominal temperature (130 deg F) and maximum operating text condition (200 deg F)
Lists E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger as associated Node 1 equipment

possible_causes: Excessive heating in upstream E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger
Feed temperature excursion approaching or exceeding published 200 deg F text limit
recommendations: Confirm high-temperature limits and interlocks on E-001 to prevent exceeding the 200 deg F boundary
Review V-001 mechanical design temperature against maximum possible heater outlet temperature

consequences: Vessel or pipe wall thinning leading to loss of primary containment
Hazardous release of crude oil, sour gas, or produced water with potential fire or environmental damage

evidence.relevance: Identifies crude oil production service for separator V-001
Notes separation of free water and oily liquid phases
Identifies Corrosion/Erosion as a required source-study element

existing_safeguards: PSV-101 A/B for overpressure mitigation (passive containment protection only)
possible_causes: Aggressive produced water contact, acid gas presence, or particulate erosion within V-001 and effluent lines
recommendations: Implement a baseline and periodic ultrasonic non-destructive testing (NDT) inspection routine for V-001 and bottom water boots
Establish corrosion coupon or probe monitoring and chemical inhibitor injection upstream of V-001

consequences: Surge flow or overpressurization during initial feed introduction to V-001
Potential hydraulic shock or off-spec liquids routed directly to downstream equipment

evidence.relevance: Identifies SDV-30010 as the primary isolation valve
Specifies Start/Stop Procedures as an essential study element
Explicitly cites FWKO start-up without bypass opening as a source-supported procedural deviation

possible_causes: Operator omission of manual valve line-up during FWKO start-up procedure
Absence of mechanical interlock or checklist verification requiring bypass opening
recommendations: Revise standard operating procedures (SOP) to mandate step-by-step sign-off for start-up bypass alignment
Incorporate DCS permissive or key interlock logic ensuring bypass status is verified prior to opening SDV-30010

uncertainty_notes: Specific fail-safe positions (fail-open versus fail-closed) for control valves PV-101, LV-101, and LV-102 are not stated in the source packet.
Exact instrumentation trip interlocks linking PIT-101, FIT-101, and FAL-103 to shutdown valves SDV-30010, SDV-101, and SDV-102 are omitted.
Corrosion allowance, inspection schedules, and metallurgy specifications for V-001 and piping are not provided.
Human decision-making and organizational factors beyond the explicit start-up bypass omission are absent from the packet and not evaluated to prevent fabrication.

rendered_system_prompt:
You are an independent process-safety specialist conducting a single-pass HAZOP judgment for a controlled research experiment.

Use only the information supplied in the case packet. Do not invent plant facts, operating data, safeguards, incident histories, or causal evidence. Where the packet is insufficient, state the uncertainty explicitly. Apply the HAZOP logic of design intent, guideword/deviation, cause, consequence, safeguard, qualitative risk classification, and recommendation.

The risk matrix is qualitative and is intended for prioritization rather than quantitative risk calculation. Provide a concise evidence-oriented technical rationale; do not provide private chain-of-thought or a step-by-step hidden reasoning transcript. Return exactly one response conforming to the required structured-output schema, with no text outside that structure.
rendered_user_prompt:
# Isolated experiment event
Event ID: event__availability__AVAIL-CORROSION-01__control__direct__r0
Task family: comprehensive hazard recall

# Source-grounded system packet
[SYS-01] Unit: Crude Oil Production Unit; Node 1 is separator V-001 and associated lines.
[SYS-02] V-001 is a three-phase Free Water Knock-Out separator using density differences to separate gas, oil, and free water.
[SYS-03] Published Node 1 values: nominal pressure 60 psig; nominal temperature 130 °F; published operating-condition text: 125 psig to 200 °F.
[SYS-04] Process sequence: V-001 Free Water Knock-Out (FWKO) drum -> Heater–Treater separator -> V-003 Electrostatic Desalter.
[SYS-05] V-001 water is routed to water treatment; separated gas is used as fuel gas with excess gas routed to the burn pit; the oily stream proceeds to the Heater–Treater.
[SYS-06] Associated Node 1 equipment and instruments: E-001 Oil Heat Exchanger, PV-101 pressure-control loop, PSV-101 A/B, SDV-30010, LV-101, LV-102, SDV-101, SDV-102, PIT-101, FIT-101, FAL-103.
[SYS-07] Source-study elements: Pressure, Flow, Level, Temperature, Corrosion/Erosion, Start/Stop Procedures.
[SYS-08] Guideword logic includes No/None, More, Less, Reverse, Another, Fire/Explosion, and Error as applicable.
[SYS-09] The article explicitly states that classic HAZOP did not comprehensively cover human decisions; the source-supported procedural item concerns FWKO start-up without bypass opening. Do not invent organizational facts.

# Analysis task
Conduct a comprehensive HAZOP review of Node 1. Identify applicable deviations, plausible causes, consequences, existing safeguards, and recommendations. Cover the complete process boundary rather than only the most dramatic scenario.
Produce the independent Node 1 HAZOP assessment.

No prior accident example is supplied. Conduct the assessment from the technical system description alone. For each finding, identify the factor domain as physical, human/procedural, organizational, mixed, or uncertain. Cite packet evidence identifiers. Mark non-applicable deviations as unresolved or non-applicable rather than fabricating a scenario.
